title: What is hosted PBX? A complete guide for small businesses
summary: Hosted PBX lets small businesses ditch expensive phone hardware. Learn how it works, what to look for, and how Zoom Phone makes switching easy.
body_markdown:
If you're still running your business on a traditional phone system, you've probably felt the pain: hardware to maintain, a phone that doesn't travel with your team, and a complicated setup that only an IT professional can touch. A hosted PBX — or hosted private branch exchange — solves all of that. Instead of hardware sitting in a back closet, your entire phone system lives in the cloud, managed by a provider, and accessible from wherever your team works. For small businesses ready to upgrade without the upfront cost and complexity of an on-premise system, hosted PBX has become the go-to solution.

## What is hosted PBX?


A hosted PBX (private branch exchange) is a cloud-based phone system that lets businesses manage calls — routing, transferring, voicemail, auto attendant, extensions, and more — without owning or maintaining physical telephone hardware on-site. The provider hosts and manages all the infrastructure remotely; you just need an internet connection and compatible devices.


In a traditional setup, a business installs PBX hardware on-site that routes calls between internal extensions and out to the public telephone network. To learn more about how that legacy infrastructure works, see our guide:[What is a PBX phone system?](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/what-is-a-pbx-phone-system/) With a hosted PBX, that same functionality moves to the cloud, delivered over the internet and accessible from desk phones, computers, or smartphones.


Cloud-based phone adoption has grown steadily among small and medium businesses over the past several years, driven by the cost and flexibility advantages of hosted systems over on-premise infrastructure.


### How hosted PBX works


Hosted PBX uses voice over internet protocol (VoIP) — the technology that transmits voice calls as data packets over the internet — to route calls through your provider's cloud infrastructure. When someone calls your business number, the call hits your provider's servers, passes through your configured rules (business hours, auto attendant, call queues, ring groups), and reaches the right person wherever they are.


### Is hosted PBX the same as cloud PBX?


For practical purposes, yes. "Hosted PBX," "cloud PBX," and "virtual PBX" all describe a phone system hosted and managed off-site by a third-party provider. Some providers make subtle distinctions between the terms, but for small businesses evaluating options, they mean the same thing: no on-site hardware, no maintenance burden, and a full-featured business phone system delivered over the internet.


## Hosted PBX vs. on-premise PBX


Feature Hosted PBX On-premise PBX


Hardware required No — hosted in the cloud Yes — servers and equipment on-site


Upfront cost Low — subscription-based High — hardware, installation, licensing


Maintenance Handled by provider Requires in-house IT or a third party


Scalability Add seats in minutes Requires hardware upgrades


Remote work support Works from any device, anywhere Typically tied to the office network


Upgrades Automatic from provider Manual, often costly


Disaster recovery Built into provider infrastructure Requires separate planning


The flexibility advantage is hard to overstate for small businesses. When your team works remotely, travels, or opens a new location, a hosted PBX goes with them — no hardware moves, no re-configuration required.


## Key features to look for in a hosted PBX system


Not all hosted PBX systems are built the same. Here's what to prioritize when comparing providers.


### Auto attendant and call routing


A good hosted PBX routes callers to the right person or department automatically — without needing a full-time receptionist on call. Look for multi-level auto attendant capabilities, business-hours routing, call queue management, and easy configuration from an admin dashboard.


### Mobile and desktop app access


Your team should be able to use the phone system from laptops, smartphones, and desk phones — all tied to the same business number. A strong hosted PBX provider offers apps across all device types so remote and hybrid teams stay connected without workarounds.


### AI-powered call tools


Modern hosted PBX systems do more than connect calls — they help your team learn from them. Look for call summaries that capture key conversation points automatically, voicemail prioritization that surfaces urgent messages first, and call questions that surface relevant insights from past conversations. These AI features — available with eligible paid plans — can save hours each week for lean teams that can't afford to miss a follow-up.


### Integrations and scalability


Your phone system should connect with the tools you already use: CRM platforms, helpdesk software, and team communication apps. And as your business grows, adding new users should take minutes, not weeks.


## Benefits of hosted PBX for small businesses


Small businesses get a disproportionate benefit from moving to hosted PBX. Here's why:


- **Lower costs.** No upfront hardware investment. A per-user monthly model means you pay for what you use and scale as you grow.
- **Professional call handling.** Auto attendants, custom greetings, and call queues give small teams the polish of a much larger operation.
- **Work from anywhere.** Calls reach your team on mobile phones, laptops, or desk phones — wherever they happen to be working.
- **Faster setup.** Many hosted PBX systems can be configured and live in a day, not weeks of IT installation.
- **Automatic updates.** Your provider handles upgrades, so your phone system stays current without any effort from your side.
- **Built-in continuity.** If your office loses power or internet, calls can route to mobile devices automatically.


## How much does hosted PBX cost?


Hosted PBX pricing follows a per-user, per-month model — a substantial shift from the large upfront hardware and installation costs of on-premise systems, which can run into the thousands of dollars before you've made a single call.


Pricing varies by provider based on included features, number of users, and whether you pay monthly or annually. Many providers offer tiered plans with basic calling at lower price points and advanced features — analytics, AI tools, compliance recording — at higher tiers. For current Zoom Phone pricing, visit the[Zoom pricing page](https://zoom.us/pricing) . For a broader look at how business phone costs stack up, see[How much does a business phone system cost?](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/how-much-does-a-business-phone-system-cost/)


## What to look for when choosing a hosted PBX provider


With many options on the market, here are the key questions to ask before you commit:


1. **Does it integrate with what I already use?** Your CRM, helpdesk, and team communication tools should connect seamlessly.
2. **Is support included — and how responsive is it?** Understand what happens when something goes wrong.
3. **How does pricing scale?** Make sure you understand per-user costs, what's included at each tier, and what triggers add-on charges.
4. **What AI features are built in?** Call summaries, voicemail prioritization, and intelligent routing can make a measurable difference for lean teams.
5. **Can I port my existing numbers?** Moving to a new provider shouldn't mean giving up your business phone numbers.
6. **What security and compliance capabilities are included?** For healthcare, financial services, or other regulated industries, compliance recording controls and data privacy features may be non-negotiable.


Some providers charge extra for AI features, compliance tools, or analytics that should come standard. Review what's actually included — not just the headline price — before you decide.

## Security and compliance with hosted PBX


Security is a real concern when moving any communication system to the cloud — and it should be part of your evaluation. Here's what to look for in a hosted PBX provider, and what Zoom Phone delivers:


- **Strong encryption in transit and at rest:** Calls, voicemails, and messages should be protected by strong encryption in transit and at rest.

For small businesses without dedicated security staff, these built-in controls take a significant burden off the team — and often exceed what a self-managed on-premise system could realistically achieve.


## Frequently asked questions


### **What is hosted PBX?**


Hosted PBX — short for hosted private branch exchange — is a cloud-based phone system where the provider manages all hardware and infrastructure remotely. Businesses get full phone system capabilities, including auto attendant, call routing, extensions, voicemail, and more, without owning or maintaining physical equipment on-site. It uses VoIP technology to deliver these features over the internet.


### **What's the difference between hosted PBX and VoIP?**


Voice over internet protocol (VoIP) is the underlying technology that transmits voice as data packets over the internet. Hosted PBX is a complete phone system that runs on VoIP technology. Think of VoIP as the engine and hosted PBX as the full vehicle. For a deeper look at how VoIP works, see[What is VoIP and how does it work?](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/what-is-voip/)


### **Is hosted PBX secure?**


Modern hosted PBX platforms offer strong encryption, E911 support, compliance-eligible configurations, and role-based access controls. For most small businesses, a reputable cloud provider delivers more robust security infrastructure than an on-premise system with limited IT resources could maintain.


### **How hard is it to switch to hosted PBX?**


Most providers — including Zoom Phone — support number porting so you keep your existing business numbers. Setup typically happens through an admin portal, and most teams are making and receiving calls within a day. There's no hardware to install and no lengthy IT project to manage.


### **Can Zoom Phone replace my current phone system?**


Zoom Phone is a full-featured hosted PBX that includes auto attendant, call routing, call queues, voicemail, SMS/MMS, compliance recording, and AI-powered call features available with eligible paid plans. For most small businesses, it replaces traditional and legacy systems entirely — while adding capabilities those systems couldn't offer. See the[Zoom Phone feature overview](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/voip-phone/features/cloud-pbx/) for the full picture.


### **What's the difference between hosted PBX, virtual PBX, and cloud PBX?**


These terms are used interchangeably by most providers and all refer to a cloud-based phone system where infrastructure is managed remotely. If you're comparing providers, focus on the features, reliability, support, and security rather than the terminology.


## Conclusion


Hosted PBX isn't just a modern alternative to traditional phone hardware — for most small businesses, it's a fundamentally better way to run business communications. Lower costs, simpler management, remote-work readiness, and AI-powered call tools that help your team do more with less: the case for staying on-premise gets harder to make every year. Zoom Phone brings all of this together in a platform your team already knows, so getting started doesn't require a project — just a plan.
